newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Inchcape Bhd sees gains from demerger.
newsitem.headline: Inchcape Bhd sees gains from demerger.

text.p: The demerger of Inchcape Bhd's marketing services businesses and its motor operations will allow the group to develop the two separate businesses better, chief executive officer Jeremy Hobbins said on Thursday. The planned demerger, announced in March, is subject to approval from the Stock Exchange of Singapore (SES) and also the company's shareholders.
Hobbins said Inchcape planned to send in a formal application to the SES by the middle of May on the proposed demerger, which would result in a new Singapore listed company.

Under the plan, Inchcape shareholders, including its parent Inchcape Plc, which owns 63 percent of the stock, would probably be given one share in the new company for every one existing Inchcape Bhd share held.
Hobbins said the planned demerger was not about "capital reduction or returning capital to shareholders".
"We have different strategies for these two businesses and we want to manage them differently," he said.
The demerger would result in Inchcape Bhd retaining its core motor and motor financing business in Singapore and Brunei and the group's other businesses will be in the new company.
The motor business accounted for 70 percent of group pre-tax profit of Singapore $79.2 million (US$55 million) in 1996.
"The motors business will see primarily organic growth. We are happy with the franchises that we have got now. We have a commanding market share and we want to optimise that business," he said.
Inchcape holds the Toyota and Suzuki franchise in Singapore and Burnei. It also has the Rover, Volkswagen and Audi franchise in Brunei.
"We will not look for new franchises. We want to grow the business through after-sales, expansion of market share and through expanding financial services in particular," Hobbins said.
The group had a lucrative motor financing business in Brunei, which it planned to expand and it was exploring similar possibilities in Singapore, he said.
The motor financing business made a pre-tax profit of S$19.7 million in 1996, up from S$15.8 million in the previous year.
Hobbins said Inchcape's used car business was thriving, though margins had not been as high as initially expected.

Under the proposed demerger, the new marketing services company would concentrate on four core areas grouped under consumer logistics, industrial businesses, branded lifestyles which includes the highly successful Salvatore Ferragamo franchise, and specialists businesses.
"We want to grow it extensively throughout the region and not just in Singapore and we are looking at joint ventures and acquisitions and alliances," he said.
Hobbins said he expected marketing services to post strong growth this year but probably not at the same rate as in 1996 which saw a 60 percent jump in profit.
